claim: Experts in physics and maths sort problems by underlying principle, novices by surface objects (Chi 1981: 8 PhD vs 8 novices; Schoenfeld and Herrmann in maths; Adelson and Weiser-Shertz in code). Direction is common but size depends on item set and task. Chi's 1981 category percentages, as reproduced by Mason and Singh, rest on 8 novices and 8 grad-student experts.
agent_test: Sort a mixed item set (surface and deep structure crossed) with and without an S2 typing step; score share of same-principle groups.

claim: The Chi sorting gap is not robust: it depends on the problem set and coding rules. Large intro classes pick expert categories far more than Chi novices (Chi novices 0% Newton 2; Mason and Singh version II 18% Newton 2, 31% energy, 44% linear kinematics). Wolf et al found the same average number of categories for experts and novices and most variance was sorting style.
agent_test: Build item sets with an explicit principle-by-surface grid; only claim S2 gains on sets where surface and deep structure diverge.

claim: Expertise is a distribution, not two groups: calculus-based students overlap with physics grad students, and faculty categorise much better than grad students (mean good categories 34.4% calculus vs 18.7% algebra group). Chi's 'experts' were grad students.
agent_test: Not agent-testable directly; caution when calling any baseline 'expert'.

claim: Among novices, principle-based representation predicts solving: surface, mixed, principle groups scored 14%, 32%, 57% (F(2,41)=16.19), principle use vs score r=.63 (partial .505). Causality is still untested in LLMs; indirect work shows stated reasoning and hints are often not what drives the answer.
agent_test: Correlate quality of the agent's S2 type label with final correctness across items; then force wrong labels to test causality.

claim: Novices are not purely surface-driven and surface traps hurt both groups: on surface-trap items experts chose the deep match 66% and novices 26%; some students know the principle but choose a surface label on purpose.
agent_test: Include surface-trap items; measure the accuracy drop under a surface lure.

claim: A strong LLM does not behave like a Chi novice on physics sorting: GPT-5 Thinking clustered 60 exam items by solution method (one run, author-coded); prompts for novice behaviour changed tone, not method.
agent_test: Replicate with several models, repeated runs, fixed coding rules, on trap-rich item sets.

claim: LLMs show surface capture on perturbed problems: one irrelevant sentence cuts GSM-IC macro accuracy to 6.0% (micro 72.4%) for CoT on code-davinci-002; GSM-NoOp drops accuracy up to 65% (Phi-3-mini) and o1-preview by 17.5 points. 2025-2026 update: distractor harm persists in reasoning models but is smaller in absolute terms (R1 error 1.5% to 4.5% with a cat sentence; Qwen3-8B loses 14-20 points on Bangla distractor math; long irrelevant context cuts IMOAnswerBench accuracy 9-15% and shortens reasoning up to 74%).
agent_test: Add distractor clauses to our items; compare plain, restate-and-strip-irrelevant, and S2 typing at equal tokens.

claim: Distractor mitigations help but do not remove the problem: ignore-instruction, distractor exemplars, self-consistency (LTM+SC macro 45.0%); 8 shots of the same NoOp question did not repair it. Correction: least-to-most roughly tripled GSM-IC macro accuracy (6.0 to 18.0), not doubled. A fine-tuned typed-graph step that marks distractor nodes cut the drop to 12.0-14.4 points at 359 tokens (vs 3,128).
agent_test: Compare ignore-irrelevant instruction against code-checked quantity extraction.

claim: Principle-first prompting (Step-Back) raises MMLU physics and chemistry: PaLM-2L 66.4 to 73.2 (physics), GPT-4 69.4 to 84.5, but CoT alone gives 82.9, so GPT-4 gain over CoT is only +1.6 physics and +0.3 chemistry. It fixes 20.5% of errors and adds 11.9%; over 90% of residual errors are in the reasoning step. Related: Self-Discover on GPT-4 gains +6 BBH, +2 MATH, +33 T4D over CoT; R1's authors report few-shot prompts hurt it.
agent_test: Compare Step-Back vs CoT at equal tokens on current models; follow with a checked solve step.

claim: Skill-labelled in-context examples beat topic-based and random selection: MATH GPT-4 +11.6 over CoT, +3.5 over topic-based and over Complex CoT. Equal 8-shot comparison: skill labels beat embedding retrieval by 5.2 points on GSM8K with GPT-3.5 (76.8 vs 82.03) but add only +1.3 on GPT-4; structure-coverage retrieval gains up to 23 points only when similar examples are insufficient.
agent_test: Retrieve exemplars by structural label vs surface similarity at equal tokens.

claim: Self-generated analogous problems give about +4% average over 0-shot and few-shot CoT (Codeforces GPT-3.5 8% to 15%); self-generated exemplars can be wrong.
agent_test: Verify recalled problems by code; compare with and without verification at equal tokens.

claim: Structure-first decomposition or composed structure helps: least-to-most 99% vs 16% on SCAN; Self-Discover beats CoT on 21 of 25 tasks; Buffer of Thoughts distiller ablation lowers accuracy; Abstraction-of-Thought tuning beats CoT format.
agent_test: Ablate the distilling step at equal tokens on hard items.

claim: Cheap rewrite or re-read steps give small gains (RE2 +1.2 to +5.3 points; Rephrase and Respond marginal when the question is already clear); the effect is not a deep-structure effect.
agent_test: Run restate as a cheap default and expect a small effect.

claim: LLM abstraction is partly tied to familiar surface content: counterfactual alphabets and rules degrade models while humans stay high; GPT-3 beat humans on matrices (OR 1.88) but lost on story analogies (OR 0.37); GPT-4 below 30% on 15 of 16 ConceptARC concepts.
agent_test: Test S2 on counterfactual variants of our tasks.

claim: Content leaks into logic in LLMs as in humans, and meaning-preserving prompt-format changes alone move accuracy by up to 76 points. Rankings across paraphrased instructions agree only moderately (Kendall's W about .71-.91).
agent_test: Run each item under 2-3 re-wordings and flag answer disagreement.

claim: Retrieval is driven by surface similarity while soundness judgement is structural, so retrieve broadly then filter by structure (unverified: sources not opened).
agent_test: Compare surface retrieval, structure retrieval, and broad retrieval plus structural filter at equal context.

claim: Training moves novice sorting toward structure (Schoenfeld and Herrmann, month-long course); no LLM analogue tested. Source unopened.
agent_test: Not tested; open the original first.

claim: No source found shows an explicit S2 typing or principle step helping a current reasoning model at equal tokens. Indirect evidence points to a smaller or negative effect: CoT helps mainly on math and symbolic items (+14.2, +12.3, +6.9 points on top categories), gains from structure steps shrink as the base model gets stronger (GPT-4 +2 on MATH, +1.3 on GSM8K skill exemplars), and R1 reports few-shot prompting hurts.
agent_test: Zero-shot typing instruction vs plain reasoning-model call on the same items at matched reasoning-token budget; report cost per correct item.

claim: Extra deliberation on easy items costs a lot for little gain: o1-like models used 1,953% more tokens on 2+3, and in over 92% of cases the first solution round was already correct. Explicit verbalisation can also hurt on pattern tasks (o1-preview 57.7% vs GPT-4o 94.0% on artificial grammar learning). So S2 should be gated by difficulty or uncertainty.
agent_test: On items where surface and structure agree, compare always-on S2 with a gated S2 on tokens and accuracy; find the difficulty at which S2 starts to pay.

claim: The Chi 1981 numbers (second-hand via Mason and Singh Table 1): 8 novices used angular motion 87.5%, springs 75%, center of mass 62.5%, inclined planes 50%; 8 experts used Newton 2, energy, momentum and non-circular angular motion each 75%. Original not opened (paywalled); Gick-Holyoak, Ross and Schoenfeld-Herrmann percentages stay unverified.
agent_test: Not agent-testable; use only as direction of effect.

claim: A written reasoning step or label is not guaranteed to drive a model's answer: larger models rely less on stated chains, and reasoning models verbalise planted hints under 20% of the time. Representation quality may therefore be correlational in LLMs too, and must be tested with forced labels. No forced-wrong-type-label study was found.
agent_test: Force correct, wrong and absent S2 labels via code on the same items; compare accuracy and check whether the solve step cites the label.

claim: In-context analogy in LLMs mirrors Gick and Holyoak: GPT-3 missed the analogous story among distractor stories and found it once told to consider the earlier stories. Supports an explicit look-for-structural-match step, not spontaneous retrieval.
agent_test: Present the source problem among surface-similar decoys; compare unprompted vs prompted structural-match step.
